text:
morgan: Heads-up — us-west1 GPU queues spiked again at 09:12 UTC, p95 latency climbing, and we got a few alerts about queue depth hitting 90% of pool capacity. spilling requests to eu-west would solve latency but egress costs are nontrivial. thoughts on policy?
jeff: saw that. current behavior is immediate cross-region spill to nearest region once local admit queue > 80%. that avoids tail latency but definitely increases egress and SLO variance.
anya: can we instead prefer model-fallback before cross-region? e.g., try quantized or 7B proxy in-region then only spill if fallback fails or pool exhausted. saves egress and likely cheaper.
infra-bot: deploy-check: routing-config v3.4 currently staged. admit_threshold=0.8, spill_policy=nearest_region, fallback_chain=[none].
sre-oncall: +1 for fallback-first. also we need to ensure SLAs for premium customers aren't impacted — they should have a reserved capacity path that won't be downgraded without explicit opt-in.
luis: technially we can do a cost-weighted decision: compute "expected_cost_delta" = egress_cost + runtime_cost_of_fallback_delta. prefer in-region fallback if expected_cost_delta < spill_cost. simple heuristic could work short-term.
morgan: that idea is good. but warning: some models' quantized variants are ~10-12% slower per token on our runtime; so fallback could still increase latency. we should check p50/p95 of each fallback option.
jeff: proposal: change admit controller to do a 2-step decision when queue > threshold: 1) evaluate in-region fallback candidates ordered by (latency_penalty, quality_penalty, infra_cost). pick first that meets quality SLA. 2) if none acceptable or local pool exhausted, allow cross-region spill with a rate cap (egress_budget) shared across tenants.
anya: can we express (1) as a config block? something like:
```yaml
admit_policy:
  threshold: 0.8
  fallback_priority:
    - model: redwood-7b-quant
      max_latency_penalty_ms: 40
      quality_drop_pct: 2
    - model: redwood-3b-quant
      max_latency_penalty_ms: 60
      quality_drop_pct: 5
  spillover:
    enabled: true
    egress_budget_per_min: 5000 # USD cents or token-eq metric
    max_spill_ratio: 0.1
```
luis: minor nit: budget as USD in config is odd. better to expose as "egress_tokens" derived from configured cost model so teams don't need currency math. but fine to start with dollars for experiments.
product-eng: we need to expose policy controls in console per-customer — so customers with strict data residency can set fallback only (no cross-region), and enterprise can enable egress allowances. also show simulated cost impact in UI.
sre-oncall: Also add a safety net: if cross-region spike would blow past global egress quota, fall back to queue-shed with informative 429 + Retry-After and recommend client-side backoff. don't silently throttle.
morgan: action items: (1) eng-platform to sketch a fallback-first admit controller PR with config like above. (2) infra to add egress_token accounting and per-pool spill caps. (3) product to spec console knobs for residency/egress. (4) SRE to draft incident runbook update for spill events. I'll pick up (1).
jeff: I'll prototype admit controller changes as a local feature flag. plan to run canary in us-west1 next week.
anya: can we add a metric "fallback_use_rate" and link it to cost dashboard? helps decide if fallbacks harm quality over time.
luis: +1. also track average latency delta and top-5 callers who triggered fallback most. might highlight hot customers to talk to about reserved capacity.
infra-bot: note: there is an ongoing node eviction test in us-west1 at 10:00 UTC — might be correlated with spike. please check test window before canary.
sre-oncall: I'll correlate spike times with eviction test and post a follow-up. if eviction is root cause we should delay canary.
morgan: thanks. small follow-up: let's make spillover max_spill_ratio default very conservative (0.02) to avoid cost surprises during initial rollout.
product-eng: noted — we'll also prepare customer comms template in case egress costs impact billing during the experiment.
jeff: will push a draft PR with unit tests and a simulated cost model by EOD tomorrow.
anya: thanks all :thumbsup:
